newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELS BACK AT WORK AFTER U.S. OPEN TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS BACK AT WORK AFTER U.S. OPEN TRIUMPH.

text.p: Ernie Els took a couple of days off to savor his U.S. Open triumph, but was back at work Wednesday to prepare for his defence of the Buick Classic at Westchester Country Club.
"Monday was a wonderful day. It was slow but I couldn't relax," said Els, who returned to his home in Orlando, Florida, late Sunday night after his one-stroke Open triumph at Congressional.
"Tuesday I lay by the pool and watched tape. It was nice having those feelings again."
The 27-year-old Els survived a four-way tussle over the last 18 holes at Congressional to beat Colin Montgomerie, Tom Lehman and Jeff Maggert for his second U.S. Open title in four years.
Els said he found last weekend's victory more satisfying than the first, when he prevailed in 1994 after a three-way playoff with Colin Montgomerie and Loren Roberts at Oakmont.
"This one was a lot sweeter. The first one I was a lot younger as a person and a player," he said.
"This one there was a lot more emotion involved. My mom and dad were there. It felt a lot more special. My goal was to win the U.S. Open. I really worked hard at it."
Els said some near misses at other major championships had whetted his desire to win another.

"After the '94 U.S. Open I had a close one at the PGA and played with John Daly in the final round at the British Open," Els said. "Maybe it was good to get close, miss a couple because I really didn't want to lose Sunday."
Els will now try to emulate Hale Irwin, a three-time Open champion, who won the 1990 U.S. Open and then returned the following week to claim the Buick Classic crown.
The big South African has a fondness for the Westchester course. He finished second and tied for fourth in two earlier appearances before his nine-stroke victory last year.
Also featured in the field will be Tiger Woods, who could not duplicate his success at the Masters. He finished in a tie for 19th place at the Open.

The young Masters champion leads the PGA Tour with three victories this year, also winning the Mercedes Championship and the Byron Nelson Classic, and is the tour's leading money winner with $1,396,466 in 11 events.
The Buick Classic could also provide a chance at redemption for Maggert, who faded down the stretch at the Open. He lost five strokes on the final six holes to finish fourth at one over par.
First prize in the tournament is $270,000.
